title: U.S. Proposes Tighter Rules on High-Tech Investments Abroad
summary:
On Thursday, October 23, the U.S. Treasury Department proposed a new rule to tighten limits on American investments in high-tech work in China, Russia, North Korea, and other countries of concern. The rule is only a proposal for now, and Treasury will hear public comments before issuing a final rule.

Outbound investment means money that U.S. investors put into companies in other countries. The government says it has worked for years to stop such investments from helping adversaries build up military power.

The proposal would expand restrictions to hypersonic systems that can travel at five times the speed of sound, supercomputing, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence, which Treasury called superintelligence. It would apply only to investments over $50,000, and it would exclude many financial investments, including stock purchases.

The program began in 2023, when then-President Joe Biden signed an order restricting outbound U.S. investments in semiconductors, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence going into China. In December 2025, Congress passed a law that codified and expanded the program to more technologies and more countries, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

Supporters say the proposal signals that Washington is tracking where U.S. capital flows and what capabilities it helps build. Craig Singleton, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said screening investments recognizes that capital can speed up military-relevant capabilities just as technology transfer can. Former trade official Ryan Majerus called the rule just the first step in a fairly long process toward stronger enforcement.

China pushed back. Its Foreign Ministry said the United States should follow market-economy principles and stop interfering in normal economic cooperation between businesses. Spokesperson Mao Ning said overstretching national security and artificially restricting trade and investment serve no one's interests.
why_it_matters: The rule could shape which technologies receive U.S. money abroad, affecting military capabilities, trade relations, and how businesses invest across borders.

background_read: An investment is money put into a company in the hope that it will grow or succeed.
An outbound investment is money that investors send to companies in other countries.
Governments sometimes limit such investments when they worry the money could help another country build military strength.
A proposal is not yet a final rule, so the public can comment on it before any final decision is made.
